comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body:
Measured 2026-08-13 against a real pane. less rings the bell instead of scrolling: it calls terminfo's smkx on startup, turning application cursor mode on, then decodes arrows as kcuu1 - ESC O A under xterm-256color. Muster sends ESC [ A because it assumes power-on state, so less echoes the sequence into its status line and beeps. vim is unaffected because its key tables accept both forms.

Paste and arrows want different answers. A paste is one action, so a socket connect per paste costs nothing and send_input can carry it today. Arrows repeat at 30+ events a second under key repeat, which is the case the latency measurement (a_26BIX28HG) has to rule on first.

Reproduce with tools/mode-cost.py - local pty, no daemon.

comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body:
Done for arrows and paste. Bare arrows resolve to a named key the daemon encodes against the pane's live modes; less scrolls, verified through the GUI. Paste goes the same way, so bracketed paste is applied from real state and a multi-line paste is text to edit rather than commands to run.

The round trip costs 0.09ms median over 20 samples, 1.6ms worst, against the 33ms a key repeat allows - so the latency worry that gated this was unfounded, and it is measured on every send rather than assumed.

Left alone deliberately: everything else in the guess was measured to survive, and each routed key costs a round trip, so the exception list stays as short as the evidence supports. herdr's key vocabulary has no pageup/pagedown/home/end/insert/delete (parse_key_combo in src/config/keybinds.rs never got aliases for them, though the KeyCodes exist), so those cannot be routed even if we wanted to - that stays part of the upstream ask a_27CTRluw7.

creator: Alexander Terp
description:
Muster encodes keystrokes locally against a guessed mode profile, because the control stream is a raw PTY write and pane modes are invisible. The two documented losses are bracketed paste and application cursor keys (arrows in vim and less).

Both are already solved server-side, on a channel we are not using. pane.send_input {pane_id, text, keys} encodes text through encode_api_text, which reads input_state().bracketed_paste and wraps the markers itself (src/app/api_helpers.rs:25-35), and encodes named keys through runtime.encode_terminal_key, the same mode-aware ghostty encoder herdr's TUI uses (:37-49, called from src/app/api/panes.rs:1508). No upstream change needed.

Two costs decide whether this is worth it, and one of them is the next card.

Latency: the JSON API socket is one request per connection, so every call pays a connect(). That is on the keypress-to-glyph path, which is exactly what a_26BIX28HG has to measure. Local encoding on the already-open control stream has no such cost.

Coverage: herdr's key-name parser refuses home, end, pageup, pagedown, insert, delete and ctrl+alt+delete (observed, corpus/herdr-0.8.0/input-path/). Arrows are accepted, so the arrow fix is available; the navigation cluster is not.

Likely shape: keep local encoding as the fast path for ordinary keys, and route the cases where the guess is known wrong - paste, and arrows if the latency allows - through pane.send_input. That is a hybrid rather than a switch, and it should be decided with the latency number in hand rather than before it.
title: Recover paste and arrow keys via pane.send_input
